items.summary: Generative AI is reshaping how research software is developed. Tools and patterns ranging from “vibe coding” through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and autonomous agents now offer compelling productivity gains, but their adoption in scientific computing surfaces failure modes that general-purpose evaluation does not catch: silent unit conversions, violated conservation laws, hallucinated physics, loss of numerical precision, and quietly broken reproducibility. These failures share a signature: nothing visible goes wrong. The AI ecosystem itself is moving fast, leaving RSEs to make consequential integration decisions with little shared vocabulary or principled guidance. This talk introduces Scientific Agentic Engineering , the central contribution of an in-progress 2026 Better Scientific Software (BSSw) Fellowship: a tool-agnostic methodology for integrating AI agents into high-stakes scientific software workflows. The framework defines how agents, scientific skills, and MCP servers should be structured around validation loops, explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and domain-specific safeguards. Every task moves through a short workflow (frame, plan and critique, implement, verify), with decisions recorded throughout, and the framework maps each documented failure mode to the stage where it is cheapest to catch. The intent is not to recommend any particular AI tool but to articulate foundational concepts that remain valid as the underlying technology changes. I will share three artifacts from the fellowship: The Framework (published July 2026). Shared vocabulary, its principles and workflow, structural guidance on where safeguards live, and a pattern catalog of named practices, each tied to the failure it counters. The Reference Workflow. A structured exercise in which RSEs use AI tools to build a small weather-model error-statistics application, applying the framework to avoid the failure modes it documents. The Community Repository. A curated starter set of scientific MCP server templates, agent skills such as unit checkers and conservation-law validators, and agent configuration examples, designed to be starting points for the community to adapt to a variety of scientific domains. These artifacts are by design community resources, and broader adoption is the explicit aim of the remaining milestones, which include an interactive online tutorial series comparing purpose-built scientific agents with general-purpose tools, a recorded live workshop published for asynchronous access, and a BSSw.io blog post directing the community to the project’s resources. This work engages the conference theme directly by advancing AI-assisted scientific software development from ad-hoc experimentation toward a disciplined, transferable engineering practice.

items.summary: Doucette rereads Keynes’s 1930 essay “Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren” as a sequencing rule, not a prophecy of mass idleness or automatic leisure. Keynes defined technological unemployment as a pace problem: labor-saving discovery outruns new uses for labor. He called it a temporary maladjustment, while predicting long-run abundance through technical progress and capital accumulation. Doucette applies this framework to the U.S. mid-2020s, focusing on generative AI’s early labor-market effects and the data-center buildout. AI stress appears mainly in junior cognitive work and entry-level hiring, not the national unemployment rate. Data centers are capital-intensive, labor-sparse operations: thousands of construction jobs, few permanent ones, and local conflict over water, power, rates, and consent. They resemble power stations or switching offices more than factories. Northern Virginia illustrates the consent problem. Keynes said little about ownership, so the paper imports distribution: who captures the dividend? It proposes three tests: absorption (rebuild the first rung), cost assignment (large loads pay incremental infrastructure costs), and the dividend (where productivity appears). It considers accelerationist, localist, and leisure-skeptic objections. Limitations include early evidence, mixed data, and one mature cluster. The conclusion separates two clocks: short-run maladjustment and long-run abundance. AI is neither a completed solution nor a surplus of workers; it changes task content and drives physical accumulation. The task is to keep entry paths open, assign costs to the load causing them, and track whether productivity reaches typical pay. Failure would be institutional, not technical.
items.title: The New Disease and the Machine Room: Keynes's 1930 Essay, Artificial Intelligence, and the Data-Center Buildout

items.summary: This record contains the preprint paper "LOST IN THE PDFS: CONTEXT DEGRADATION AND PARAMETRIC HALLUCINATIONS IN LLM UIS" , authored by Gabriele D’Iorio (University of Naples Parthenope).  The study investigates the structural limitations and operational vulnerabilities of commercial web-based Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces when handling long, multi-document sequential workflows in educational contexts. Abstract: The growing use of LLMs for educational purposes, especially by inexperienced users, inevitably leads to LLMs hallucinating and making mistakes. This study presents an experiment using the web version of Gemini (Pro Standard and Flash Standard modes) to simulate a numerical analysis class covering three topics (interpolation, piecewise interpolation, and approximation), each in a separate PDF. This study is subdivided into two scenarios created to evaluate how the LLM responded and, above all, to see how long it took to hallucinate or suffer from context degradation. The results demonstrate the failure of both scenarios due to context degradation. Despite large theoretical context windows, sudden attachment truncation in the web UI forces the model to rely on its parametric memory, leading to severe hallucinations and sycophantic behavior. Key Topics Covered: - Context Degradation & "Lost in the Middle" Phenomenon: Analysis of how LLMs lose retrieval accuracy in prolonged sessions. - Parametric Hallucinations: How models compensate for context loss by fabricating details from pre-training data. - Document Parsing Challenges: Visual layout issues in standard Web UIs. - Experimental Evaluation: A comparative analysis of a single-chat setup (Scenario A) versus a dual-agent/tutor setup (Scenario B). Data Availability: The comprehensive dataset, interaction logs, prompt configurations, and Python scripts used for token counting are openly accessible in the project’s GitHub repository at: https://github.com/gabpolymath/lost_in_the_pdfs/
items.title: Lost in the PDFs: Context Degradation and Parametric Hallucinations in LLM UIs

items.summary: Adaptability release: the analysis pipeline no longer assumes an NV-scale emitter or a negligible instrument response, and measured data enter through a documented file contract. This release also upgrades the fit physics itself -- two changes that came out of adversarial re-examination rather than feature work. Bring your own emitter and instrument load_hbt_csv / save_hbt_csv : a documented two-column contract ( delay_ns,counts ) with an exact round trip and refusals for wrong headers, field counts, negative counts and non-increasing delay axes. Configurable lifetime windows : t1_bounds / t2_bounds (ns) on analyze_histogram , fit_g2_histogram and profile_likelihood_ci -- validated on entry. The defaults are the NV-scale window used since v0.1. The test suite runs a tau1 = 0.15 ns, tau2 = 5 ns emitter and shows BOTH halves: the default window fails visibly (error > 0.2), the emitter's own window recovers g2(0) to better than 0.05. register_platform (existing) plus a test that a user-defined platform runs the whole pipeline; load_fisequr now takes the dataset directory explicitly instead of defaulting to one machine's path. The fit physics, corrected Physical parameterization. The LM fit and the profile likelihood now fit the dip depth rho^2 multiplying BOTH exponentials (g2(0) = 1 - rho^2), the form g2_measured itself uses. The previous 1 - d e1 + a e2 form capped d at 1 -- which biased g2(0) upward for any emitter with a strong bunching shoulder -- and hid a genuine (d, a) ridge behind that cap. The instrument response is in the model. Both fitters now use the closed-form Gaussian-convolved exponentials at cfg.sigma_irf , so the estimand is the IRF-free g2(0), not the softened dip the raw histogram shows; a test constructs a case where the two differ by more than 0.02 and checks the right one is recovered. An honest interval, and the knob that tightens it. With the normalization free, a slow bunching shoulder trades almost exactly against the flat level -- a real near-degeneracy of the histogram alone (probed directly during development: the exact-Poisson likelihood is flat to Delta NLL ~ 1 from g2 = 0.10 to 0.30 in the demonstration case). The profile interval now says so by being wide. The information that breaks the tie is the independently measured singles rate: pass r_hat from the counters and c0_prior=(1.0, sd) at their precision, and the interval tightens to what the data genuinely support (covering the truth and shrinking ~2.7x from 10 s to 60 s in the tests). Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated) CSV contract: exact round trip; four distinct malformed-file refusals. Fast-emitter recovery only with its own window, and visible failure without it. IRF-aware estimand: the profile CI covers the IRF-free g2(0) where the IRF-softened value is more than 0.02 higher. Profile CI with the singles-rate prior: covers the truth at 10 s and 60 s, width shrinks by more than 2x; with the normalization free it stays covering but wider -- the degeneracy is reported, not hidden. Window validation: malformed bounds raise in both fitters. 67 tests across Python 3.9-3.13 (ML tests skip without torch). Install: pip install -U sparq-triage .
items.title: SPARQ: spiking physics-in-the-loop autonomous reinforcement triage of quantum emitters

items.summary: Patinae v0.5.0 Zawinski's law says that programs keep expanding until they can read email. Patinae started as a molecular viewer. It now has background tasks, Markdown output, and an AI plugin that can connect to MCP servers. We appear to be one mail server away from compliance. The largest change in 0.5.0 is underneath all of that: the task system has been completely rebuilt around one shared lifecycle . Loading a structure, running a script, and asking a plugin to do background work now use the same rules for completion, progress, errors, and cancellation. Those rules extend across the desktop application, native plugins, IPC, Python, and the web viewer. That gives plugins the foundation for longer workflows. A plugin can issue a command, receive its actual result, wait for any background work it starts, and decide what to do next. The new AI plugin puts that into practice: ask for a scene in ordinary language, let the agent operate Patinae, and have it inspect the rendered image before answering. Highlights A task has one lifecycle, wherever it starts Background work now receives a host-assigned task ID and stays under the shared task runner's control. Progress, diagnostics, final outcomes, and cancellation requests belong to that task. The desktop shows active tasks with progress and cancellation controls, and services background work independently of rendering. The distinction between accepting a command and finishing its work is explicit. An immediate command returns its result. A command that starts background work also returns task IDs, which clients can observe, wait for, or cancel. Success means the required scene changes have been applied; it does not promise that the GPU has already presented a frame. Scripts and plugin workflows can create child tasks. A parent stays active until its children finish, and cancellation propagates through the task tree. Cancelling stops further work cooperatively; changes already applied to the scene remain. A wait timeout ends the wait without cancelling the underlying task. Python command methods wait for background work by default, so a script can fetch a structure and then operate on it. Use wait=False to get task IDs immediately and manage them through tasks or a notebook viewer's view.tasks . Browser integrations receive command results and use viewer.tasks.get , list , wait , and cancel to follow the same lifecycle. Plugins can coordinate work and recover from errors Plugins now receive typed replies to the host commands they issue, correlated to the original request and delivered only to the requesting plugin. Replies include success or failure, output messages, and every accepted task ID. A command can fail after starting some work, so those IDs remain available for inspection. For plugin authors, the new contract separates responsibilities clearly: The host owns task identity and state. A plugin submits a task request and starts its worker after the host accepts it and delivers the assigned ID. Workers report progress, output, and completion. Scene mutations go through the host and must be acknowledged before the plugin reports success. Nested commands belong to the parent task. Their completion and cancellation participate in the same lifecycle. Recovery can be deliberate. Child failure fails the parent by default. An executor can opt into deciding the parent outcome after inspecting and handling a failed child. The original failure remains in task history. This matters for an agent that needs to correct a command, or a script that has a fallback when a download fails. The parent can handle the error and continue while preserving the record of what happened. Silent execution also follows the task tree. It suppresses REPL presentation while retaining results, diagnostics, and logs, so a plugin can handle intermediate failures without filling the output panel with messages it intends to recover from. Polling plugins additionally receive named selections and Recent Atoms path

items.summary: Abstract Background Dapsone is a key component of multidrug therapy (MDT) for Hansen's disease but is associated with serious adverse effects, including methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and hepatotoxicity. The simultaneous occurrence of these complications is rare and potentially life-threatening. Early recognition is critical, especially in resource-limited settings where advanced diagnostic tools may not be readily available. Case Report The patient presented with jaundice, fever, and breathlessness approximately one month after initiation of dapsone therapy. Examination revealed pallor, icterus, and edema. Laboratory findings showed severe hyperbilirubinemia (>25 mg/dL), elevated transaminases, anemia (hemoglobin ~8 g/dL), markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase (1705 U/L), and negative Coombs test, consistent with non-immune hemolysis. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and arterial blood gas analysis indicated metabolic acidosis. Methemoglobinemia was clinically diagnosed by the treating team. Imaging revealed pleural effusion and ascites, suggesting systemic involvement. Dermatology consultation suggested dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome, and dapsone was discontinued. The overall findings were consistent with dapsone-induced multisystem toxicity involving hepatic, hematological, and respiratory systems. Conclusion This case highlights a rare but severe presentation of dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and acute liver failure. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for dapsone toxicity in patients presenting with jaundice, anemia, and respiratory symptoms shortly after initiation of therapy. Early drug withdrawal and prompt supportive management are essential to prevent life-threatening complications.
items.title: Dapsone-Induced Hemolytic Anemia, Severe Acute Liver Injury and Clinically Suspected Methemoglobinemia in a Patient with Hansen's Disease: A Rare Case Report.

items.summary: 2.2.0 A minor version, not a patch: the change below alters what a default run leaves on disk. Nothing about your results, final outputs or logs changes, but a default that deletes files users previously got to keep is more than a patch. Changed Intermediate pfiles are now deleted as the run progresses, at defaults. Each QC step reads a genotype file and writes a new one — callrate reads your input and writes …_callrate , sex reads that and writes …_sex , and so on — so a ten-step run creates ten copies of your data. At GP2 release scale each copy is tens of GiB. Cleanup used to be skipped whenever warn_only was set, and warn-and-continue is the default , so at defaults every copy survived for the whole run. The only way to reclaim the disk was --no-warn , which also turns warn-and-continue into fail-fast — so you could not have both. That is a bad trade on a long run, where warn-and-continue exists precisely so an eight-hour job does not die on one recoverable step. The two flags no longer interfere: | | before | now | |---|---|---| | (default) | keeps every copy | deletes each copy once the next is written | | --full-output | keeps every copy | keeps every copy | | --no-warn | deletes + fail-fast | fail-fast only | | --no-warn --full-output | keeps + fail-fast | keeps + fail-fast | --full-output is now the only switch governing retention; --no-warn is purely failure policy. Peak disk during a run drops from roughly one working copy per step to one overall — on the round-19 full-GP2 run, ~98 GiB written against a ~50 GiB peak. If you relied on the old default to inspect intermediates, pass --full-output — it reproduces the previous behavior exactly. A failed step's input is still kept either way, so a broken run can still be examined.

items.summary: We propose the Encephlian Standard Format (ESF), a 19-channel international 10–20 montage at 250 Hz, average re-referenced, microvolt-calibrated, and channel-wise robust z-scored, as a deterministic canonical representation for deploying pretrained EEG classifiers on heterogeneous acquisition hardware, paired with a recoverability framework that predicts which signal-level shifts ESF can and cannot recover. On the Temple University Abnormal EEG Corpus (TUAB, n = 276 patient-stratified, 253 unique patients), a frozen EEGPT linear probe attains clean AUROC 0.908. We sweep five acquisition-shift axes (native sampling rate, per-channel gain, 50 Hz line noise, electrode montage, and broadband signal-to-noise) and show that left-invertible and bandwidth-preserving operators are (f,0)-recoverable while sub-Nyquist sampling and broadband Gaussian noise are not (Propositions 1, 2). A Pinsker-based AUROC–total-variation bound holds on 18/18 measured axis-arms (median implied constant 0.10). items.summary: 2.2.0 A minor version, not a patch: the change below alters what a default run leaves on disk. Nothing about your results, final outputs or logs changes, but a default that deletes files users previously got to keep is more than a patch. Changed Intermediate pfiles are now deleted as the run progresses, at defaults. Each QC step reads a genotype file and writes a new one — callrate reads your input and writes …_callrate , sex reads that and writes …_sex , and so on — so a ten-step run creates ten copies of your data. At GP2 release scale each copy is tens of GiB. Cleanup used to be skipped whenever warn_only was set, and warn-and-continue is the default , so at defaults every copy survived for the whole run. The only way to reclaim the disk was --no-warn , which also turns warn-and-continue into fail-fast — so you could not have both. That is a bad trade on a long run, where warn-and-continue exists precisely so an eight-hour job does not die on one recoverable step. The two flags no longer interfere: | | before | now | |---|---|---| | (default) | keeps every copy | deletes each copy once the next is written | | --full-output | keeps every copy | keeps every copy | | --no-warn | deletes + fail-fast | fail-fast only | | --no-warn --full-output | keeps + fail-fast | keeps + fail-fast | --full-output is now the only switch governing retention; --no-warn is purely failure policy. Peak disk during a run drops from roughly one working copy per step to one overall — on the round-19 full-GP2 run, ~98 GiB written against a ~50 GiB peak. If you relied on the old default to inspect intermediates, pass --full-output — it reproduces the previous behavior exactly. A failed step's input is still kept either way, so a broken run can still be examined.

items.summary: The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua’s altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel’s unfinished offering, Cain’s failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is also tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses; the original connection-density test was performed on a pre-set group of 124 verses selected by the narrative. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place , the observed network produced Z = 19.37 (p < 0.0002) against 5,000 random permutations. A second, deliberately simpler test removes the seven control letters א, מ, ת, נ, י, ה, ו from every word and performs direct string matching with no root database; it still yields Z = 10.29 (p < 0.0002) , with the same major long-range connections rising to the top. A raw-word test remains significant at Z = 5.17 (p = 0.0013) . A separate anthology comparison tests whether similarly chosen biblical themes automatically generate the same effect. The Ebal/Shechem axis reaches Z = 17.35 , compared with Covenant Z = 10.07 , Jerusalem/Temple Z = 1.60 , Joseph Z = −8.13 , and Tabernacle Z = −7.16 . A scientific appendix further examines comparative anatomical and genomic parallels associated with one of the essay’s most unexpected motifs, while explicitly distinguishing scientific observation from midrashic interpretation. After fifteen years of work, the author does not regard this as a story invented to fit the text, but as part of a larger architecture that the text itself gradually disclosed — a structure he considers himself fortunate to have uncovered, even if only in part, and to place on record now. items.summary: Abstract Background Dapsone is a key component of multidrug therapy (MDT) for Hansen's disease but is associated with serious adverse effects, including methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and hepatotoxicity. The simultaneous occurrence of these complications is rare and potentially life-threatening. Early recognition is critical, especially in resource-limited settings where advanced diagnostic tools may not be readily available. Case Report The patient presented with jaundice, fever, and breathlessness approximately one month after initiation of dapsone therapy. Examination revealed pallor, icterus, and edema. Laboratory findings showed severe hyperbilirubinemia (>25 mg/dL), elevated transaminases, anemia (hemoglobin ~8 g/dL), markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase (1705 U/L), and negative Coombs test, consistent with non-immune hemolysis. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and arterial blood gas analysis indicated metabolic acidosis. Methemoglobinemia was clinically diagnosed by the treating team. Imaging revealed pleural effusion and ascites, suggesting systemic involvement. Dermatology consultation suggested dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome, and dapsone was discontinued. The overall findings were consistent with dapsone-induced multisystem toxicity involving hepatic, hematological, and respiratory systems. Conclusion This case highlights a rare but severe presentation of dapsone-induced methemoglobinemia, hemolytic anemia, and acute liver failure. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for dapsone toxicity in patients presenting with jaundice, anemia, and respiratory symptoms shortly after initiation of therapy. Early drug withdrawal and prompt supportive management are essential to prevent life-threatening complications.

items.summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justifiably verify from the evidence and resources available to it? This paper organizes the question around distinct boundaries of identification, generation, computation, implementation and correspondence. For a declared space of possibilities and an evidence map, exact verification is possible precisely when the demanded claim is constant on each evidence fiber. A local version characterizes sound answers at a particular observation and separates unresolved evidence from observations outside the declared model. Computation or recursive generation based solely on unchanged evidence cannot distinguish possibilities that evidence leaves indistinguishable. The paper separates semantic support from effective computation and resource-bounded attainment. In explicitly presented finite classes, it develops adaptive acquisition, relational candidate selection, safe revision composition and finite-machine attainment results under declared operational contracts. It distinguishes pointwise availability from uniform implementation and identifies conditions under which abstraction and execution preserve the guarantees being claimed. Probabilistic continuation is treated through explicit probability assumptions and attainable guarantee regions; ideal convex mixing is distinguished from mixtures realizable under hard resource limits. Contextual equivalence for declared continuation systems preserves both demanded guarantees and metadata. These results support a structured verification record that distinguishes established answers, insufficient evidence, computational exhaustion, unavailable implementations, unresolved authority and model inconsistency. The routing protocol is sound under its stated assumptions rather than a universal classification of every possible failure. The framework also separates correctness within a model from evidence that the model represents a concrete system, including the verifier itself. Its contribution is a synthesis of exact conditions, impossibility witnesses and attainable constructions that makes the boundaries of justified verification explicit without converting internal coherence, agreement or successful execution into an unsupported claim about reality.

items.summary: Patinae v0.5.0 Zawinski's law says that programs keep expanding until they can read email. Patinae started as a molecular viewer. It now has background tasks, Markdown output, and an AI plugin that can connect to MCP servers. We appear to be one mail server away from compliance. The largest change in 0.5.0 is underneath all of that: the task system has been completely rebuilt around one shared lifecycle . Loading a structure, running a script, and asking a plugin to do background work now use the same rules for completion, progress, errors, and cancellation. Those rules extend across the desktop application, native plugins, IPC, Python, and the web viewer. That gives plugins the foundation for longer workflows. A plugin can issue a command, receive its actual result, wait for any background work it starts, and decide what to do next. The new AI plugin puts that into practice: ask for a scene in ordinary language, let the agent operate Patinae, and have it inspect the rendered image before answering. Highlights A task has one lifecycle, wherever it starts Background work now receives a host-assigned task ID and stays under the shared task runner's control. Progress, diagnostics, final outcomes, and cancellation requests belong to that task. The desktop shows active tasks with progress and cancellation controls, and services background work independently of rendering. The distinction between accepting a command and finishing its work is explicit. An immediate command returns its result. A command that starts background work also returns task IDs, which clients can observe, wait for, or cancel. Success means the required scene changes have been applied; it does not promise that the GPU has already presented a frame. Scripts and plugin workflows can create child tasks. A parent stays active until its children finish, and cancellation propagates through the task tree. Cancelling stops further work cooperatively; changes already applied to the scene remain. A wait timeout ends the wait without cancelling the underlying task. Python command methods wait for background work by default, so a script can fetch a structure and then operate on it. Use wait=False to get task IDs immediately and manage them through tasks or a notebook viewer's view.tasks . Browser integrations receive command results and use viewer.tasks.get , list , wait , and cancel to follow the same lifecycle. Plugins can coordinate work and recover from errors Plugins now receive typed replies to the host commands they issue, correlated to the original request and delivered only to the requesting plugin. Replies include success or failure, output messages, and every accepted task ID. A command can fail after starting some work, so those IDs remain available for inspection. For plugin authors, the new contract separates responsibilities clearly: The host owns task identity and state. A plugin submits a task request and starts its worker after the host accepts it and delivers the assigned ID. Workers report progress, output, and completion. Scene mutations go through the host and must be acknowledged before the plugin reports success. Nested commands belong to the parent task. Their completion and cancellation participate in the same lifecycle. Recovery can be deliberate. Child failure fails the parent by default. An executor can opt into deciding the parent outcome after inspecting and handling a failed child. The original failure remains in task history. This matters for an agent that needs to correct a command, or a script that has a fallback when a download fails. The parent can handle the error and continue while preserving the record of what happened. Silent execution also follows the task tree. It suppresses REPL presentation while retaining results, diagnostics, and logs, so a plugin can handle intermediate failures without filling the output panel with messages it intends to recover from. Polling plugins additionally receive named selections and Recent Atoms path

The opinion explicitly links this risk to three structural features often associated with Masonic practice: an oath of allegiance, an obligation of secrecy, and inter‑member solidarity—each of which can undermine public confidence in the judge’s neutrality. ---  The invisibility problem and informational asymmetry --- A distinctive contribution of the opinion is its focus on invisibility. Unlike family ties, professional networks, or financial interests, Masonic membership is typically not verifiable by litigants.  This informational asymmetry prevents parties from invoking standard procedural safeguards (e.g., recusal motions grounded in disclosed relationships), thereby magnifying the appearance risk.   The CDJ effectively treats non‑disclosable affiliations that entail strong internal loyalties as structurally suspect, because they remove the very mechanism—transparency—that allows objective impartiality to be tested and preserved. --- Constitutional and convention tensions --- While the opinion builds on existing case law, it surfaces unresolved tensions with fundamental rights: - Freedom of association and conscience: Judges retain associative rights, and any limitation must be proportionate and necessary in a democratic society.  - Proportionality and legal certainty: Because the CDJ’s opinions are not binding law and cannot by themselves create statutory incompatibilities, the practical force of the guidance relies on its authority and on how disciplinary bodies and courts receive it. Unlike family ties, professional networks, or financial interests, Masonic membership is typically not verifiable by litigants.  This informational asymmetry prevents parties from invoking standard procedural safeguards (e.g., recusal motions grounded in disclosed relationships), thereby magnifying the appearance risk.   The CDJ effectively treats non‑disclosable affiliations that entail strong internal loyalties as structurally suspect, because they remove the very mechanism—transparency—that allows objective impartiality to be tested and preserved. --- Constitutional and convention tensions --- While the opinion builds on existing case law, it surfaces unresolved tensions with fundamental rights: - Freedom of association and conscience: Judges retain associative rights, and any limitation must be proportionate and necessary in a democratic society.  - Proportionality and legal certainty: Because the CDJ’s opinions are not binding law and cannot by themselves create statutory incompatibilities, the practical force of the guidance relies on its authority and on how disciplinary bodies and courts receive it. items.summary: This manuscript addresses consciousness within this framework by first adopting a specific, defensible philosophical position — dual-aspect monism — after identifying and rejecting two internally contradictory earlier framings, then developing a two-part structural-and-functional criterion for identifying physical systems engaged in unified information processing, anchored to real, independently-published quantitative thresholds. We derive an exact power-law memory-decay result from the same underlying network structure the criterion itself is based on. This manuscript does not claim to resolve the philosophical “hard problem” of consciousness, and states this limitation explicitly. The foundational architecture, geometric intuitions, and motivating philosophy of this framework originated independently with the author prior to and separate from any AI involvement. Subsequent mathematical derivation, connection to established physics literature, computational verification, and error-checking were conducted through extended technical work with AI systems (Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini). The author directed this process, evaluated and selected among proposed derivations, and takes full responsibility for the accuracy and originality of the final work.

items.summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
items.title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

items.summary: A 0.1° monthly and daily terrestrial water storage anomaly (TWSA) product for the Ganga (Ganges) River Basin, 2000–2025 , together with the source code, the inputs, and the full evaluation record that produced it. GRACE and GRACE-FO JPL RL06 mascons are spatially downscaled by fitting a predictor–TWSA relation across mascons; every mascon's area-weighted aggregate is then forced back onto the observed value. The monthly field is disaggregated to daily under an exact monthly constraint, its within-month shape supplied by the ERA5-Land water balance with nothing fitted at the daily scale. Per-pixel uncertainty is reported as four separate terms rather than one number, because only some of them are measurable against an observation. What changed in v1.0.1, and what did not. The data are unchanged. The three product netCDFs, the monthly and daily COGs, the trend field and every input and intermediate archive are the same files already in this record — if you have them, there is nothing to download again, and any analysis built on v1.0.0 stands. Four files change, all of them code or documentation: grace-grb-1.0.1.zip , the source at the new tag, which adds main/trend_regions.py and the scripts behind three manuscript figures; evaluation_tables.zip , which gains trend_by_region.csv ; figures.zip , which gains those three plates; and DATA_README.md . The version exists for reproducibility rather than revision: the regional trend figures quoted in the paper were computed from a region definition that had never been committed, so a reader holding the archived trend field could not reproduce them. That definition is now in the archive, it is checked to partition the basin, and the paper cites this version. What is imposed and what is learned. Each mascon's level and linear trend are taken from GRACE rather than learned from the predictors — the secular signal here is groundwater abstraction, and no reanalysis simulates pumping. Only the sub-mascon anomaly is modelled, from 78 predictor features built on ERA5-Land and nine covariates, seven of them static and two annual cropland fractions held constant after 2022. Mass conservation then forces every mascon mean back onto the observation by a minimum-norm correction. Agreement with GRACE at mascon scale is therefore arithmetic, not evidence of skill : the basin mean of this product reproduces the GRACE basin mean at r = 1.00000, RMSE 0.27 mm. We state that plainly so it is not mistaken for validation. Held-out performance. Skill is reported only where it can be measured — at spatial units the model never saw, at times it never saw, and against an independent observation. Spatial (leave-one-mascon-out, 19 folds with a neighbour buffer): RMSE 88.2 mm, R² 0.638, NSE 0.635 over 83,309 held-out cell-months. Cluster bootstrap over mascons (2,000 resamples): RMSE 82.1–95.1 mm, R² 0.580–0.694. Temporal (whole months held out): interior gap-filling RMSE 71.7 mm (R² 0.775); scattered months 74.5 mm (0.713), a random split and so optimistic — each withheld month keeps its neighbours in training; out-of-record extrapolation 91.1 mm (0.730) . The last is the regime the post-2024 months live in. Independent (656 quality-controlled CGWB dug wells): at basin scale the downscaled field reaches r = 0.814, RMSE 57.0 mm against a bilinear-interpolation baseline at r = 0.742, RMSE 73.1 mm. Skill is strongly scale-dependent: median R² is 0.48 per mascon but 0.19 per well, and NSE exceeds zero at only 168 of 656 wells. Neither side is ground truth — a well is a point head times an estimated specific yield, the product a 0.1° cell from a 3° mascon — so the scale dependence is reported as the result rather than a single pooled number. items.summary: This dataset provides a harmonized global collection of river discharge (Q), suspended sediment concentration (SSC), and suspended sediment load (SSL) observations for source-traceable sediment-data analysis and model evaluation. It integrates observations from multiple monitoring networks, regional datasets, literature compilations, and satellite-derived products, with standardized metadata, coordinates, temporal information, variable definitions, and units. Missing sediment variables are derived where appropriate, gauge locations are linked to MERIT-Basins river reaches and upstream drainage units, and variable-level quality flags are provided to distinguish good, derived, suspect, bad, and missing values. Provenance information is preserved so that released records can be traced to their contributing source stations and datasets. The release consists of three complementary components. The main station-reference component contains 7,135 unique stations and 2,997,121 records from 17 source datasets spanning 1912–2025, distributed as separate daily, monthly, and annual station-by-time NetCDF products according to source-reported temporal support. The climatology auxiliary component contains 1,361 stations from five sources and provides long-term or climatological Q, SSC, and SSL information, with reported source coverage extending from 1884 to 2017. The satellite-derived auxiliary component contains 38,550 locations and 16,478,276 records from three source datasets spanning 1984–2020 and provides complementary spatial coverage, mainly for SSC. The archive includes the daily, monthly, and annual NetCDF products; climatology and satellite-derived auxiliary NetCDF products and their accompanying query catalogues; station, source-station, and source-dataset catalogues; and dataset documentation. The catalogues preserve station-level and source-level provenance and support station screening, source tracing, and reproducible use of the released products. The main station-reference component is intended for station-level time-series extraction, source-traceable benchmarking, and evaluation of hydrological, river-routing, erosion, sediment-transport, and land-surface models. The climatology and satellite-derived components provide complementary long-term and spatial context and should not be treated as direct substitutes for the time-resolved station-reference products. Daily, monthly, and annual products represent different temporal support and should be selected according to the requirements of each analysis rather than combined without accounting for observation coverage. This dataset is intended as a reusable and extensible community resource. Future releases may incorporate additional observations and improvements to the harmonization and integration framework while preserving versioned releases for reproducibility.
items.title: A Harmonized Global Station-Reference Dataset of River Discharge, Suspended Sediment Concentration, and Suspended Sediment Load

items.summary: Adaptability release: sqzcomb now speaks laboratory units and fits measured data, so the normalized-units engine underneath is usable directly from an experiment. Added sqzcomb.physical : the exact dictionary between laboratory ring parameters and the package's normalized LLE frame. RingSpec (loaded linewidth in Hz, escape efficiency, single-photon Kerr shift, pump wavelength -- with a mandatory reference naming where the numbers come from) plus normalized_pump , threshold_power , normalized_detuning , normalized_dispersion , normalized_frequency / physical_frequency , and intracavity_photons . Conventions are checked by identities rather than trusted: every conversion round-trips exactly, F scales as sqrt(P), and threshold_power is cross-validated through the package's own flat-state cubic -- at the returned power, homogeneous_steady_states contains the rho = 1 root to machine precision. Physical constants come from scipy.constants ; no constant is typed by hand. sqzcomb.fitnoise : extraction of (mu, eta, kappa) from measured homodyne noise spectra in dB relative to shot noise -- the standard characterization of a below-threshold squeezer. fit_noise_spectra fits the package's own input-output model (the same code path as sqzcomb.spectra , cross-checked in the tests against the independent closed form) to the squeezed/antisqueezed trace pair, with an optional white dark-noise floor and per-point measurement sigmas enabling a chi-square consistency check. Identifiability is enforced, not hoped for: one quadrature alone is a single Lorentzian with two shape numbers for three unknowns, so the single-trace fit is refused unless an independently measured kappa_hz is supplied; an antisqueezed trace systematically below shot noise is refused as unphysical. Changed scipy is now a declared dependency (the new modules use scipy.constants and scipy.optimize.least_squares ). Anchors (asserted in tests/test_adapt.py , not stated) Conversion round trips exact to 1e-15; F(4P) = 2F(P); at fixed eta_esc, doubling kappa halves F. threshold_power hits the rho = 1 root of the package's own cubic for alpha in {0.7, 1.0, 1.8}. Noise-free synthetic spectra return the generating (mu, eta, kappa) to better than 1e-6; the fitted model equals the closed form S = 0.5[1 -/+ 4 eta mu / ((1 +/- mu)^2 + Omega^2)] at every frequency to 1e-10. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted parameters matches the reported one-sigma uncertainties; a dark floor deliberately omitted from the model biases eta, and fitting it recovers the truth. The under-determined single-trace case and the impossible below-shot-noise antisqueezed trace are refused with explanatory errors. Full test suite: 80 passed. See CHANGELOG.md for details.

items.summary: Chapter 6 : Sandboxing With BRICS Frame --- Now, chapter 6: sandboxing this dis|mis main capacity using the BRICS frame. First, what is BRICS?  B for Brazil, R for Russia, I for India, C for China, S for South Africa, at the time of writing.  While wandering through the streets of Madrid, I talked to caballeros from the street who said those people are heroes. That was a discourse we were not used to in our homeland. We had not the same sources of disseminated information.  Which are usually secondary sources of information, privately owned. And we are not talking about this as a potential conflict of interest, in the benefit-of-the-doubt sense, on those privately owned secondary sources of information for us.  So that was an opening. You see... what is fantastic in sublimation is that an a priori violation of our fundamental rights that would leave from the autumn to so much brightness and summer light in our life, hopefully. In the previous chapter, we started by stressing this mean-means fallacy, that is to say, a bad loop for a five-year-old child.  And the potential conflict of interest of private editors who are, well, editing hard or soft information and communication techniques, and sometimes undermining our mindfulness.  That is to say, less than 20 percent of our potential.  An interrogation:  Would it make sense to use emotion and motion, dance, visual arts, visual recensions, music to acquire as well as express, whether or not that makes sense in the legal, technical, informational, or court space?  So, being able to get out of the box using back-and-forth lateral thinking, thanks to symbolic thinking, using Trinity lecturing in a dis|mis main case, helped us find ways of expression and reconciliation, and opened a highway of recensions, openings such as DDEF, DEFI, like finance, for instance, up to the personal level, oration and recension, using accessible means within this mean-means fallacy. items.summary: Frequency-shift corrections are applied in deep-space navigation as a catalogue of formulas: common offsets, detector-end $O(c^{-3})$ cross terms and the nonlinear Doppler bias are re-derived for every mission and every data type. This paper derives the structure itself, from a single transitivity axiom. Under that axiom the endpoint factor of any light-path observable is a ratio of generators --- the \textbf{Fuxi value} $\FX_{A\|B}=\alpha_A/\alpha_B$ --- multiplied by a path factor; the generator is identified with the rate of proper-time flow, $\alpha_X=\mathrm d\tau_X/\mathrm dt_{\rm GalST}$. The resulting framework (Fuxi-ratio Mapping Theory, hereafter FMT) leaves the path-dependent transfer factor $\Pi_{\rm TTF}$ with the full complexity of the null-geodesic boundary-value problem, while its $1$PN expansion reproduces the standard frequency-shift formulas term by term at $O(c^{-2})$ and endows the IAU conversion constants $L_C,L_G,L_B$ with a direct generator interpretation. Three consequences are closed-form. \textbf{(i)} The projected pulsar-Doppler residual is \emph{exactly} linear in the relativistic velocity $\mathbf u\equiv\gamma\mathbf v$: the $O(c^{-3})$ kinematic term of the coordinate-velocity parameterization is a parameterization effect with the exact closed form $v_D^3/(2c^2)\,\hat{\mathbf v}_D$, removable in one analytic step, and \emph{identically absent} under $\mathbf u$. \textbf{(ii)} Isotropic and dipolar residual components are absorbed exactly --- the latter as a velocity error independent of the pulsar number and of the network geometry. \textbf{(iii)} Residuals of angular order $\ell\ge2$ are \emph{not} absorbed; their leakage is fixed by the higher moments of the pulsar directions, so precision and bias immunity are governed by different moments of the same network. Velocity identifiability is necessary and sufficient: the pulsar directions must not be cocircular. Model-internal consistency tests with a realistic 16-pulsar IPTA geometry reach $16.1\ \mu$m/s (three-axis RMS) at ideal timing precision $\sigma_\delta=10^{-13}$, and a full Earth-departure-to-Mars-surface arc is closed by the same expression with only its inputs changed. Both statements are model-internal limits: the term-by-term agreement with the standard formulas is limited to $O(c^{-2})$, the velocity figures presuppose an ephemeris residual $\delta C_P\lesssim3\times10^{-14}$, and practical accuracy is bounded by clock, ephemeris and direction knowledge. FMT modifies neither general relativity nor observational hardware: it is an algebraic interface callable on existing ephemerides and timing data.

items.summary: Adaptability release: sqzcomb now speaks laboratory units and fits measured data, so the normalized-units engine underneath is usable directly from an experiment. Added sqzcomb.physical : the exact dictionary between laboratory ring parameters and the package's normalized LLE frame. RingSpec (loaded linewidth in Hz, escape efficiency, single-photon Kerr shift, pump wavelength -- with a mandatory reference naming where the numbers come from) plus normalized_pump , threshold_power , normalized_detuning , normalized_dispersion , normalized_frequency / physical_frequency , and intracavity_photons . Conventions are checked by identities rather than trusted: every conversion round-trips exactly, F scales as sqrt(P), and threshold_power is cross-validated through the package's own flat-state cubic -- at the returned power, homogeneous_steady_states contains the rho = 1 root to machine precision. Physical constants come from scipy.constants ; no constant is typed by hand. sqzcomb.fitnoise : extraction of (mu, eta, kappa) from measured homodyne noise spectra in dB relative to shot noise -- the standard characterization of a below-threshold squeezer. fit_noise_spectra fits the package's own input-output model (the same code path as sqzcomb.spectra , cross-checked in the tests against the independent closed form) to the squeezed/antisqueezed trace pair, with an optional white dark-noise floor and per-point measurement sigmas enabling a chi-square consistency check. Identifiability is enforced, not hoped for: one quadrature alone is a single Lorentzian with two shape numbers for three unknowns, so the single-trace fit is refused unless an independently measured kappa_hz is supplied; an antisqueezed trace systematically below shot noise is refused as unphysical. Changed scipy is now a declared dependency (the new modules use scipy.constants and scipy.optimize.least_squares ). Anchors (asserted in tests/test_adapt.py , not stated) Conversion round trips exact to 1e-15; F(4P) = 2F(P); at fixed eta_esc, doubling kappa halves F. threshold_power hits the rho = 1 root of the package's own cubic for alpha in {0.7, 1.0, 1.8}. Noise-free synthetic spectra return the generating (mu, eta, kappa) to better than 1e-6; the fitted model equals the closed form S = 0.5[1 -/+ 4 eta mu / ((1 +/- mu)^2 + Omega^2)] at every frequency to 1e-10. Seeded Monte-Carlo scatter of the fitted parameters matches the reported one-sigma uncertainties; a dark floor deliberately omitted from the model biases eta, and fitting it recovers the truth. The under-determined single-trace case and the impossible below-shot-noise antisqueezed trace are refused with explanatory errors. Full test suite: 80 passed. See CHANGELOG.md for details.
